title.narrative: Share-Net Colombia 2021-24

description.narrative: Share-Net International es una plataforma de gestión de conocimiento en salud sexual y reproductiva (SSR) y derechos sexuales y reproductivos (DSDR), se compone de redes de conocimiento nacional en diferentes países (como Share-Net Colombia) las cuales permiten la generación, traducción y divulgación de conocimiento e investigación. Share-net reúne la experticia y fortalezas de diferentes organizaciones holandesas, socios y actores internacionales clave que trabajan en SSR y DSDR para alcanzar los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible relacionados con DSDR y VIH y también estimula la participación de socios internacionales, regionales y nacionales clave en temas de DSDR.

description.narrative: Cross-country learning

comment.narrative: *Course on �Care for GBV victims� and �Psychological first aid:� these courses were officially offered to the SN-CO members, but some members of the secretariat also participated.*Excel training: Profamilia our host organization offered virtual training on three levels for Excel. Two members of the secretariat are currently enrolled/cursing the trainings.*SHIRIM 2022-23 Trainings in Ethiopia:Sustainability: institutional development, quality service provision, and financial sustainability. From the Dr Getachew Bekele presentation �Knowledge platform sustainability: reinforcing and reframing discourse� we learned about different models of knowledge and the community engagement continuum. SN Jordan: including non-traditional means to SN activities that can transform mutual learning, this was done through a game consisting of explaining SRHR concepts without using certain words. SN Burundi "spider in a network": shared how they developed a contextualized Theory of Change to scale up the joint efforts of SN Burundi and SRHR Solutions, and also, how are they broadening to other topics such as WASH and nutrition sectors.SN Burkina Faso: meaningful youth engagement. How they carried out trainings in AFP/SMART, a youth advocacy method developed in Western Africa.SN Ethiopia: design thinking and how to reframe problems into challenges and opportunities and root causes into assumptions.SN Netherland: member engaging experiences and results of different strategies.SN Bangladesh: Non-verbal communication is: expressions, touch, the voice tone, speed and volume.Social and Behavior Change Communication - SBCC: the stages of change theory, theory of planned behavior theory, and the diffusion of innovation theory.Inclusivity: as part of the reviewing the inclusivity paper activities; co create a definition of inclusivity.

*Profamilia, our host organization, hired and carried out a 4-session course on �Easy reading� or Text Adaptation. Two members of the SN-CO secretariat participated in the course where they learned about generalities for text translation and adaptation. They shared this knowledge with the secretariat, and we obtained tools and tips to make texts easier to read for everyone, but more importantly, easier to read for specific populations (e.g. people with physical or cognitive disabilities).*Collecting Success Stories Session: We attended a SNI session where we learned about Success Stories, what is a success story, how to write one and why do we use success stories in the M&E report.*Introduction training modules SN: Before the current secretariat members were hired, two representatives of the Profamilia Research Department attended the training modules for SN, after that the materials and information were shared with the secretariat, this included a general framework of what is and how Share-Net works, some information about Share-Net International and the other national hubs, and also about the work proposal for Share-Net Colombia (Being hosted by Profamilia).*SHIRIM: As part of the SHIRIM process we attended workshops and capacity building sessions on communications, decolonizing, meaningful youth participation, human rights approach, and fundraising.*Fundraising: Our coordinator, Diana Carolina Pe�a, attended a training on fundraising organized by Share-Net international with other organizations from the Latin-American region, which was led by Han Valk Fundraising Consultancy.*NVivo basic training: For the development of the SHIRIM research we identified the necessity to strengthen our abilities in the data analysis processes, because of this we hired an expert for a three-session training on NVivo, the data analysis software.

Psychological First Aid Course. The three sessions were carried out on June 15, 22 and 29. Feminist edge. Our coordinator and M&E analyst had the privilege of participating in this year�s cohort of the Feminist Edge course, thanks to the support of SNI.

SHIRIM trainings:*Knowledge translation, knowledge generation, knowledge use differences.*System thinking approach: Iceberg model, fishbone model, socio-ecological model.*Sensitive subject in challenging context � Elizabeth Sully, PhD. Strategies to acknowledge cultural, social, and political settings of the places we work in.*Reframming � Karim Benammar. Think differently or make things differently.*Dealing with opposition and the use of the �movable middle� concept.*Generating insights. Break insights to actionable pieces, rethinking our framework and being aware of our assumptions.*Safety Tools by Justice for Prosperity. Safety regarding filed work, handling data, technology, etc.*Deep Democracy as an inclusive dialogue method.*Tools and games to challenge our way of thinking (values and norms).*Juncture Game � Advocacy exercise. Put ourselves in different roles to understand the advocacy process.

We believe that the activity that provided us with the greatest amount of learning was the Knowledge Translation Fund and the development of the Regional Knowledge Translation Fair: The intention to involve community-based organizations and provide resources to those who need it most must be accompanied by the recognition that their needs go beyond financial resources, we now know that organizations require technical accompaniment processes at different levels, logistical flexibility, and in many cases capacity building spaces. This should be included and considered from the design of ToR in proposals calls. The planning of international events requires a significant investment of time from the entire staff, this can be alleviated with the hiring of a temporary expert in event planning.

comment.narrative: 3 state of the art for 3 CoP, and 1 product from the SHIRIM- Change Package

(3) State of the Art documents for each CoP: As part of the preparation tasks in the CoP building process, we carried out three documental reviews and analysis on each CoP. -Abortion and Voluntary Termination of Pregnancy: we included and analyzed 62 articles/papers-Gender-Based Violence: we included and analyzed 123 articles/papers-Sexuality, Health, Rights and Ageing: we included and analyzed 112 articles/papers.All the documents are currently in the layout process with our designer.(2) Change Package: In the beginning of the SHIRIM process we aimed to develop a document with guidelines for a communications strategy containing the perspectives of young people interested in SRHR and other related topics. We wanted to establish these guidelines because they would be an important resource when we started building our own Share-Net Colombia communications strategy, but also, the document with these guidelines could be a resource for other work groups like the CoPs. For this we conducted several focus groups and interviews, this gave us more information and resources than expected, so at the end of the SHIRIM, the research resulted in two products instead of the original goal:o(1) document with Guidelines for a communications strategy for youth. This was the original target of the SHIRIM � Change Package product. The document presents the results of a process of co-construction and exploratory research with youth-led organizations, from which some general guidelines necessary for a communication proposal aimed at adolescents and young people in the region are glimpsed. (add link)o(1) document with the Research Report from the process carried out with the youth-lead organizations. The report presents the results of different consultation spaces with youth-led organizations. In these spaces (focus groups and interviews) qualitative and quantitative data was collected about their communication and dissemination priorities on sexual and reproductive health and rights. (add link)

*Statistical Note on Menstruation in Colombia with DANE (National Administrative Department of Statistics), the Family Compensation Fund of Antioquia - Comfama and Share-Net Colombia.*Rio Rivers research proposal on conscientious objection

The two products that were planned for the year only reached the design phase and took longer than expected: research on perspectives on sexuality in older adults and research on digital sex work. These are processes that are still ongoing and will be continued in 2024.In addition, we contributed to a third Profamilia research funded by the Rio-Rivers Foundation on the provision of abortion services in Colombia, but the data collection phase was not successful in 2023 and is under redesign.

Yet to be published: an article that consolidates the findings of the focus groups conducted on the access and quality of information and education on SRHR for LGBTIQ+ population, this product has not yet been published

Finally, our coordinator attended a meeting with the new Ambassador representative where all the work and progress of our hub was shared.

We had three meetings with the embassy representative during the year in April, October and November to discuss the activities we had developed as well as the perspective of the embassy on the alliances or new members we could approach.The ambassador of The Netherlands in Colombia, Ernst Noorman, also participated in the opening session of the CCC where he shared his thoughts on how quality information on SRHR was key to continue advancing together in the access to SRHR for all people.Finally, during the visit of some of our secretariat to the Hage in The Netherlands in October, our Coordinator participated in a meeting with Joris W.P. Jurri�ns, head of the Health and AIDS division, where they discussed some of the MoFA priorities regarding regional expansion and the positioning of our knowledge platform with donors and allies.

We have had two meetings with Martha Arevalo from the embassy, one in the beginning of the year (January) to discuss our workplan and another one in April along with Maria Codina from SNI to talk about the future of our platform.? We also partnered with the embassy to host a donors� breakfast during our Regional Knowledge Exchange Fair where we invited potential donors and other embassies to present our platform. Support was also provided to Martha Arevalo to include the achievements of our platform in the latest report of the embassy (august).

We held three meetings with the representative of the Netherlands Embassy in Colombia Martha Arevalo, where we presented the Share-Net Colombia project and discussed how the embassy could be involved in our activities. She also attended our launch event, where we agreed on her participation in our Steering Committee as observers.

comment.narrative: *Proposal for AMAZE Global Impact Awards.*Proposal for doing the knowledge management for the Latin-American hub of the Family Planning 2030 initiative.

We presented an expression of interest to the Equality Fund along with our member organization Barranquilla +20. Along with Share-Net Netherlands, Share-Net Bangladesh and The Broker we applied to the research grant from Sexual Violence Research Initiative. Also in alliance with KIT, SNI and Share-Net Burundi we presented a proposal to the French Agency of Development. The Research Office of Profamilia applied for funding with a research proposal on sex work, which was an initiative of the CoPs on GBV and LGBTIQ+.

comment.narrative: At the end of the year, the implementation of the FP2030 began with exploratory meetings to define the knowledge management activities Share-Net Colombia will provide. We expect this to be fully developed and with financial impact on 2024.

The Research Office from Profamilia signed a contract with Saldarriaga Concha Foundation to complete a research on stigmas and perceptions around sexuality for old people and their caregivers.?The research is a CoP initiative, is currently being developed and SNCO secretariat is providing technical support. Family Planning 2030: We are currently working together with Save The Children for the global association of Family Planning in LATAM region hub. We created a CoP on Contraception and Family Planning, besides contributing and co-creating other activities such as webinars and the regional fund on SRHR for civil society and youth and community-led organizations.
